_doc: A lit indicator, by day and by night (the traffic's lane changes and turns: doc/port.md, traffic): the clock run 10 s so traffic is out, then the vehicle on a turn nearest the town's centre that shows its turn's indicator (setViewNear signalling: the clock stopped, the side to be lit and the heading printed), from 30 degrees up, from its front quarter (40 degrees from its heading: its front and its right side, both headlamps in view) and from the opposite rear quarter (220: its rear and its left side, both tail lamps in view), so the lens that flashes and the one that does not are in the same picture. At 150 px a metre a lens of 6 cm is 9 px and the whole vehicle is in the frame (at 60 it was 250 px long round the middle; at 250 from 12 degrees the rig, which looks at the vehicle's middle, left its lamps under the frame). The lens flashes (render/materials.json agents signal_hz 1.5, signal_duty 0.5: 0.667 s a flash, lit half of it): each view is shot three times, a shot 1.14 s after the other as measured (0.71 of a flash), so of the three at least one has it lit and one dark. Then the player's usual view of a street (16 px a metre, from 75 degrees up and from behind along the vehicle's own heading: the sight line comes down over the street the vehicle drove, where a view across the block was hidden by a tower): there a lens of 10 cm is under 2 px, and a lit one is kept signal_least_px (4) wide by the shader (render/materials.json agent, agents.gdshader lens_grow), so the flashing dot at the vehicle's corner is found by eye. The same at 22 h.
